extracted.intended_audience: military officers and administrators responsible for post exchanges, departmental legal/advisory staff, and government accountants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing the establishment, management, custody of funds, liabilities, membership, property, and procedural handling of military post exchanges under War Department regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer duty of care in handling funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of care properly required of an officer in charge when entrusting funds or duties to subordinates (e.g., sending steward to bank vs personally attending deposit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If officer fails to take proper degree of care and loss occurs (steward appropriates funds), officer is responsible (C. 13867, Jan. 2, 1903). But where reasonable trust is required in ordinary business operations (e.g., entrusting first sergeant to obtain change while commander sick) and there was no reason to suspect desertion/theft, officer may not be held responsible (C. 29057, Oct. 3, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody rules for non-public 'bakery fund'
rubrics_metrics.description: Bakery fund is a Government instrumentality and not public money; the officer in charge may be relieved by competent authority from responsibility for a loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping the bakery fund in a government-provided safe (lock combination known only to limited officials) was proper care; officer not required to keep it in bank. Replacing the fund from private funds immediately after loss does not prevent later requesting relief (C. 15609, Dec. 15, 1903).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability when using subordinates for cashing vouchers
rubrics_metrics.description: If an officer, for convenience, sends a private (or subordinate) to cash a voucher and the private deserts with money, loss should be borne by the officer vis-à-vis the post exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: officer sent private to cash $18.50 voucher; soldier deserted — loss borne by officer (C. 28866, Aug. 25, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility timing for daily receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Under paragraph 337 (1895 regs), the officer in charge is not responsible for that day's receipts until they are turned over to him by the steward on the following morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no evidence of negligence or want of precaution on officer's part, officer not legally liable for loss of receipts taken before turnover (P. 58,437, Mar. 28, 1893).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and reporting on loss of exchange funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 318 (1908 regs) requires careful investigation and reporting by the post council with recommendations as to responsibility, for decision by the department commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If post is outside department command (e.g., Alcatraz), report should be forwarded to The Adjutant General (C. 24380, Feb. 6, 1909).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and reexamination of department commander's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 317 does not provide for an appeal from the department commander's decision on loss of funds; however, Secretary of War may reexamine before ordering stoppage of pay under statutory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where officer held responsible and has not replaced funds, Secretary of War may reexamine before ordering pay stoppage under section 1766, R.S., as amended (O. 20003, July 5, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement by stopping pay
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer's pay may legally be stopped to reimburse a company fund for amounts owing to the fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: where deceased officer left unendorsed government check equal to company fund shortage, recommendation was to stop $360 against pay due the deceased and cancel the check (C. 7957, Apr. 7, 1900).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on purchases/contracts with military persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 593 (1904 regs) prohibits officers/agents purchasing supplies for Government from persons in military service or contracting with them; but this prohibition is directed at persons, not at post exchanges (which are instrumentalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post exchange being a government instrumentality, the prohibition was held not to apply; exchanges may, for example, repair government typewriters or do laundry work for Government charging reasonable compensation (C. 17927, June 15, 1905; C. 18156, Oct. 31, 1905).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of exchange profits and disposition on muster out
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits from a post exchange are considered to belong to the organization as such and not to individual enlisted men composing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a company operating an exchange mustered out, surplus held to belong to the organization; funds should be applied to benefit enlisted men or to company/regimental funds as best subserves Government interests (C. 11089, Aug. 29, 1901; 10917, Jan. 25, 1902).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of balances when exchanges close or restructure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an exchange is entirely closed out and a new, distinct exchange comes into existence, balances may be turned over to the new exchange if it has voluntarily assumed certain debts of the old exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: $75 balance turned over to new exchange that assumed unknown debts of the old one after four years (C. 17463, Feb. 8, 1905).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of debts/assets of non-permanent organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Debts or assets belonging to exchanges operated by non-permanent organizations (e.g., hospital detachments) should be turned over to appropriate departmental authority for proper application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A debt from a deceased member assigned as detachment dividend to surgeon in command should be turned over to the chief surgeon of the department for application to a proper beneficiary when detachment ceased (C. 19321, Mar. 10, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of accumulated special funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Accumulated small funds (e.g., prison mess funds) upon return or reorganization should be distributed to appropriate units or locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: $500 in prison mess fund from Cuban Pacification recommended distributed between military prisons at Fort Jay and Fort Leavenworth (C. 24686, Mar. 23, 1909).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of post exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Post exchanges are governmental instrumentalities established under War Department regulations (not necessarily by direct legislation) and are subject to War Department control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are maintained for troop welfare, discipline, and recreation; recognized by commissioners and afforded exemptions (e.g., special tax exemptions) and may be supported by Congressional appropriations for buildings, etc. (Dugan v. U.S. and cited authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational form and treatment of donated articles
rubrics_metrics.description: A post exchange is a voluntary unincorporated cooperative association of organizations (companies/detachments); articles donated to the exchange are assets of the association to be accounted for and turned over to successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donated articles considered part of exchange assets and pass to successor organizations (P. 65,127, May 26, 1894; O. 27964, Mar. 6, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance to exchange officer from exchange funds
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no legal objection to allowing the post-exchange officer an allowance out of exchange funds to offset pecuniary risk undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowance may be made to offset risk the officer assumes in managing exchange funds (G. 3108, Apr. 15, 1897).

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation in name of the exchange officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the post exchange is an unincorporated association managed by an Army officer, litigation on behalf of the exchange should be in the name of the exchange officer as exchange officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case precedent: Dugan v. U.S. — action brought in name of exchange officer (G. 19268, Mar. 1, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to legal counsel for exchange matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange officers may apply for legal advice under paragraph 1005 and, in proper cases, request assistance from Department of Justice or appropriate U.S. attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where contemplated litigation against a corporation or special counsel needed, request may be made for government legal assistance (G. 19268, Mar. 1, 1906; G. 20279, Apr. 20, 1907).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal liability of exchange officer to creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation as 'exchange officer' and responsibility for management does not by itself make the officer personally liable to unpaid creditors of the exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officer may become personally responsible only if he assumes personal responsibility for the debt or by conduct causes creditor to lose right to recover from the exchange (G. 27964, Mar. 6, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal acquittal does not negate financial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquittal of an exchange officer by court-martial on embezzlement charges does not relieve him from financial liability for shortages he made good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officer who made good shortage and was acquitted could not recover refunded amount; court-martial pertains to discipline, not financial accounting (O. 17934, May 5, 1905).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on general banking services by exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Doing general banking business (accepting deposits for safekeeping) is not among the purposes of a post exchange and is not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post exchange may not accept soldier deposits for safekeeping (O. 11155, Aug. 31, 1901).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation on exchange revenue activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revenue-raising activities (e.g., collecting a dog tax) which impose important restrictions on military/police administration are not within the scope of exchange-sourced revenues unless clearly covered by orders/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such proposed taxes recommended not authorized as outside exchange scope (G. 27317, Sept. 30, 1910).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit policies and officer responsibility for failure to charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable credit may be given to officers by the exchange; indebtedness of soldiers may be collected on pay rolls even if credit exceeded authorized limits. Officers who fail to charge such debts appropriately may be held to make good losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: officer's failure to charge soldier's debt on pay rolls led to officer being required to reimburse exchange (G. 10298, Mar. 18, 1911; C. 14828, Dec. 26, 1903).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility and officers' liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership in post exchange consists of organizations (companies/detachments); officers are not eligible for membership and therefore are not liable for exchange debts by virtue of officer status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officers of post where exchange located are not liable for its debts (C. 19533, Jan. 7, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared responsibility for losses by council and officers
rubrics_metrics.description: When losses result from prolonged neglect or mismanagement, all officers responsible (e.g., exchange officer and post exchange council) should be held liable for the loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: losses over two years due to neglect held council and officer responsible (C. 26516, Apr. 14, 1910); failure to compel payment for six months led to liability (C. 20869, Jan. 11, 1907).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on erection, ownership, and repair of exchange buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Post exchange may erect suitable temporary buildings when sufficient funds available; permanent structures on reservations require Secretary of War authority; repairs/alterations borne by exchange when Quartermaster cannot provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Secretary of War authorized erection without Government cost (except doors/windows supplied), building treated as exchange asset; unauthorized additions to public buildings become U.S. property; licensed buildings removable if removal yields excess above damages, otherwise become U.S. property (O. 10034, Oct. 15, 1901; A. 10305, May 14, 1901).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity principle for dividends and entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Dividends due to organizations forming an exchange remain payable to those continuing organizations even if certificate or deposit was issued to an exchange officer during bank suspension/resumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dividend due in 1896 paid in 1903 to organizations continuing as members (C. 14928, July 8, 1903).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of organizations for exchange obligations on dissolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where exchange cannot pay obligations (e.g., organizations have been ordered away and exchange dissolved), the several organizations comprising the exchange remain liable for obligations incurred on the joint account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reimbursement to officer who involuntarily paid suppliers by the organizations comprising the exchange at time indebtedness was incurred (C. 27964, Mar. 6 and Oct. 3, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of new members and finality of account adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Before admitting a new organization, a board of officers must examine and adjust exchange affairs and values; the department commander's action is intended to be final except in cases of fraud or discovery of facts that could not have been known with due care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fraud/new facts are shown, department commander may appoint a board to investigate and recommend equitable settlement (C. 19178, Feb. 9, 1906; C. 19248, Mar. 6, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of dividends relative to organization size
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership is by organization but exchange regulations consider the size of the organization: size on joining taken from number present at joining, while dividends are calculated on the basis of the whole number present during the distribution period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: detachment reduced from 12 to 6; dividends distributed on basis of 6 in accordance with regulations (C. 20043, July 11, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness of exchange membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership in an exchange is not obligatory on units forming the garrison; organizations may choose to join or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated directly: membership is voluntary (C. 19248, Mar. 6, 1906).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification of detachments as exchange members
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlisted men detailed for a long course of instruction who occupy separate quarters and have a separate mess may constitute an organization eligible to acquire exchange membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Artillery School detachment of year-long instruction constituted an organization competent to join (C. 29351, Jan. 4, 1912).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple exchanges and branch establishments permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no legal objection to establishing one exchange with several branches at a post or to several independent exchanges at the same post (e.g., regimental exchanges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted by regulation and decisions (C. 27345, Oct. 11, 1910).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment/readjustment of accounts with paymasters
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts between paymasters and post exchanges may be ordered readjusted where errors (e.g., overpayments) are discovered, even if membership has changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: paymaster who overpaid may have accounts readjusted with exchange; discovery after membership changes does not bar readjustment (C. 24167, Dec. 2, 1908).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and approval of post exchange council proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 318 requires that the 'proceedings' of the post exchange council be submitted to post commander for approval/disapproval; 'proceedings' means the record of the action taken by a majority of the council, not a minority report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the commander approves only a minority report (rather than the council proceedings), that does not comply with regulations (C. 29268, Nov. 28, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may receipt for dividends when exchange officer dies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dividend becomes payable and the exchange officer who held funds dies before distribution, a regimental adjutant or appropriate officer may properly receive and receipt for the dividends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when exchange officer died before dividend declared, regimental adjutant may receive and receipt (C. 16517, June 28, 1904).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of government property to exchange at cost
rubrics_metrics.description: A government bureau may legally transfer property to a post exchange at cost price, as exchanges are recognized governmental agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted by precedent (C. 20993, Jan. 26, 1907).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraph costs and use of government lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of telegraphic messages over commercial lines for exchange business are not lawfully chargeable to public appropriations for public business; exchange messages should be transmitted free over War Department-owned lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telegraph costs for exchange business borne by exchange or transmitted free over Department lines (C. 19479, Mar. 26, 1910).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for paymaster computation errors when exchange acts as agent
rubrics_metrics.description: When the exchange acts simply as an agency to cash final statements and the paymaster later discovers an overpayment due to his own error, the exchange should not bear the loss; the soldier is the debtor and the paymaster should seek reimbursement from him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange customarily advances partial payment as accommodation without profit and relies on paymaster's check as officially accurate; loss from paymaster error should not fall on exchange (case discussed near end of text).
